environment.database.DB_MYSQL_HOST: Host of an external MySQL or MariaDB database. It is used only when the host, user and name are all set, and it wins over PostgreSQL.
environment.database.DB_MYSQL_NAME: Name of the MySQL or MariaDB database. Needed together with the host and user.
environment.database.DB_MYSQL_PASSWORD: Password of the MySQL or MariaDB database.
environment.database.DB_MYSQL_PORT: Port of the MySQL or MariaDB database.
environment.database.DB_MYSQL_USER: User of the MySQL or MariaDB database. Needed together with the host and name.
environment.database.DB_POSTGRES_HOST: Host of an external PostgreSQL database. It is used only when the host, user and name are all set and no MySQL or MariaDB database is configured. Without either, the built-in SQLite database is used.
environment.database.DB_POSTGRES_NAME: Name of the PostgreSQL database. Needed together with the host and user.
environment.database.DB_POSTGRES_USER: User of the PostgreSQL database. Needed together with the host and name.
environment.database.ENABLE_PRERUN: Runs the scripts in /data/prerun/*.sh before NPMpro starts.
environment.database.INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL: E-mail address of the first administrator, created at the first start. Remove it afterwards.
environment.database.INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSW: Password of the first administrator, created at the first start. Remove it afterwards.
environment.database.INITIAL_DEFAULT_PAG: Default site for the first start: 404, 444, redirect, congratulations or html. Without it, congratulations is used. Remove it afterwards.
environment.goaccess.GOA: Turns on the GoAccess log report. Also turns on Write log files. Without it, the GoAccess report setting in Logs & monitoring applies.
environment.goaccess.GOACLA: Command line arguments for GoAccess. Without it, NPMpro builds them from the GoAccess settings in Logs & monitoring; set, it wins and locks those settings. GeoLite2 database arguments are added automatically for the databases in /data/goaccess/geoip.
environment.modules.NGINX_LOAD_NJS_MODUL: Loads the njs (JavaScript) module and the QuickJS engine.
environment.modules.NGINX_LOAD_VHOST_TRA: Loads the virtual host traffic status module.
environment.modules.PHP83_APKS: Extra PHP 8.3 packages to install, separated by spaces. Each name must start with php83-. Turns PHP 8.3 on.
environment.modules.PHP84_APKS: Extra PHP 8.4 packages to install, separated by spaces. Each name must start with php84-. Turns PHP 8.4 on.
environment.modules.PHP85_APKS: Extra PHP 8.5 packages to install, separated by spaces. Each name must start with php85-. Turns PHP 8.5 on.
environment.modules.PHP_APKS: Extra packages installed once for all PHP versions, separated by spaces. Each name must start with php-. Needs PHP83, PHP84 or PHP85 turned on.
environment.network.DISABLE_H3_QUIC: Turns HTTP/3 (QUIC) off. Forced on while the PROXY protocol is on for HTTPS.
environment.network.DISABLE_IPV6: Turns IPv6 off for nginx and the web UI.
environment.network.ENABLE_MPTCP: Adds multipath (Multipath TCP) to the listeners of the web UI, the HTTP and HTTPS hosts and the streams.
environment.network.HTTPS_PORT: Port nginx listens on for HTTPS and HTTP/3. While HTTP is on, it must differ from the HTTP port.
environment.network.HTTP_PORT: Port nginx listens on for HTTP.
environment.network.IPV4_BINDING: IPv4 address nginx listens on for HTTP and HTTPS.
environment.network.IPV6_BINDING: IPv6 address, in square brackets, nginx listens on for HTTP and HTTPS.
environment.network.LISTEN_PROXY_PROTOCO: Expects the PROXY protocol on both the HTTP and HTTPS listeners.
Expects the PROXY protocol on the HTTP listener.
Expects the PROXY protocol on the HTTPS listener. This turns HTTP/3 off.
environment.network.NC_AIO: Nextcloud All-in-One mode: at start, creates a proxy host for the Nextcloud domain to 127.0.0.1:11000 with a new certificate (unless the domain is already used), and turns HTTP off unless DISABLE_HTTP is set.
environment.network.NC_DOMAIN: Domain of the Nextcloud All-in-One proxy host. Required while Nextcloud All-in-One mode is on, it must contain a dot.
environment.network.NGINX_QUIC_BPF: Turns on the nginx QUIC eBPF routing (quic_bpf) for HTTP/3.
environment.network.NPM_IPV4_BINDING: IPv4 address the web UI listens on.
environment.network.NPM_IPV6_BINDING: IPv6 address, in square brackets, the web UI listens on.
environment.network.NPM_LISTEN_LOCALHOST: Makes the web UI listen on localhost only (127.0.0.1 and [::1]).
environment.nginx.NGINX_DISABLE_TLS12: Turns TLS 1.2 off, so only TLS 1.3 is accepted.
environment.nginx.NGINX_FORCE_X25519MLKE: Allows only the X25519MLKEM768 key exchange and turns TLS 1.2 off.
environment.nginx.NGINX_LOG_NOT_FOUND: Logs requests for files that do not exist (log_not_found).
environment.nginx.NGINX_TRUST_RSA_PKCS1: Also accepts the rsa_pkcs1 signature algorithms, which are off by default.
environment.nginx.NGINX_TRUST_SECPR1: Allows the secp256r1, secp384r1 and secp521r1 curves for the key exchange. Turned off when only X25519MLKEM768 is forced.
environment.nginx.NGINX_WORKER_CONNECTIO: Maximum connections per nginx worker process.
environment.nginx.NGINX_WORKER_PROCESSES: Number of nginx worker processes, or auto for one per CPU core.
environment.users.PGID: Group ID NPMpro runs as. 0 runs as root. Set PUID as well.
environment.users.PUID: User ID NPMpro runs as. 0 runs as root. Set PGID as well.
environment.users.TZ: Time zone of the container, for example Europe/Berlin. Without it, the time zone setting in Advanced applies (UTC by default).

settings.certificates.default-certificat: Served for requests to host names NPMpro has no host for and on the web UI port. Built-in uses a generated placeholder certificate.

settings.certificates.ech-interval.hint: {min} to {max} hours between runs of your ECH script (/data/tls/ech/cron.sh). Only used when the script is not empty.
settings.certificates.key-size.hint: The curve for ECDSA (secp384r1 recommended) or the number of bits for RSA (4096 recommended).
settings.certificates.key-type.hint: ECDSA is recommended (smaller keys, faster handshakes). Choose RSA only for clients that cannot use ECDSA.
settings.certificates.must-staple.hint: Marks new certificates as must-staple and keeps OCSP stapling on. Only for CAs that support it (ZeroSSL); Let's Encrypt refuses such requests.
settings.certificates.ocsp-stapling.forc: Stays on while OCSP Must-Staple is on.
settings.certificates.ocsp-stapling.hint: Sends the OCSP response along with certificates from the ACME server, when the CA offers OCSP (Google Trust Services, ZeroSSL). Turns TLS certificate compression off.
settings.certificates.profile.hint: The certificate profile requested from the ACME server, checked with the server when you save. Keep empty for the server's default profile. With Let's Encrypt, shortlived is the default; clients that require a Common Name do not work with shortlived and tlsserver certificates.
settings.certificates.profile.invalid: Up to 64 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores
settings.certificates.renewal-interval.h: {min} to {max} hours between renewal checks. A certificate is only renewed when it is due.

settings.environment.note: These variables are read when the container starts and cannot be changed here. To change one, edit your compose file (or container template) and recreate the container. Values of passwords, e-mail addresses and keys are never shown.
settings.forward-auth.anubis-images.hint: Shows your own images from /data/anubis (happy.webp, reject.webp and pensive.webp) on the Anubis challenge pages.
settings.forward-auth.intro: Default upstreams for proxy hosts that use forward authentication (Auth Request under Options on the host's Details tab).
settings.forward-auth.upstream.hint: Used by proxy hosts with {provider} that have no upstream of their own; a host's own value wins. scheme://host:port or scheme://cu_name, without a path. Keep empty for none.
settings.geoip.account-id.invalid: The account ID is a number of up to 10 digits
settings.geoip.account.hint: You need a free MaxMind account and a license key (Account, Manage license keys).
settings.geoip.background: The databases are being downloaded in the background. The status below updates when the download is done.
settings.geoip.edition.asn.hint: Networks (AS number and name) for the network lists
settings.geoip.edition.city.hint: Optional, cities for GoAccess. A much larger download.
settings.geoip.edition.country.hint: Countries for the map, the country lists and nginx country rules
settings.geoip.intro: NPMpro downloads the free MaxMind GeoLite2 databases itself and looks up countries and networks on this server, so visitor IPs are never sent anywhere. A separate geoipupdate container is not needed.
settings.geoip.secret-error: The saved license key cannot be decrypted, enter it again
settings.geoip.update-now.hint: Downloads the databases now with the saved account. NPMpro also updates them every 3 days.
settings.geoip.update-now.needs-account: Save an account ID and a license key first.
settings.logs.goaccess.anonymize.hint: Masks part of each visitor IP in the report (--anonymize-ip). Level 1 hides the last IPv4 byte (the last 64 bits of IPv6), level 2 two bytes (80 bits), level 3 three bytes (96 bits).
settings.logs.goaccess.drop-query-string: Removes the query string from the URLs in the report (--no-query-string), so tokens in URLs are not stored.
settings.logs.goaccess.hint: Runs GoAccess, a web log report for admins under /goaccess. GoAccess reads the log files, so Write log files stays on while it runs. The GOA variable wins over this setting.
settings.logs.goaccess.keep-days.hint: {min} to {max} days. How long GoAccess keeps the data of its report (--keep-last).
settings.logs.goaccess.real-os.hint: Shows the full operating system version instead of only its family (--real-os).
settings.logs.goaccess.resolve-hosts.hin: Looks up the host names of visitor IPs for the report (--with-output-resolver). This sends DNS queries for them.
settings.logs.goaccess.title: GoAccess
settings.logs.rotations.hint: {min} to {max}. How many rotated log files are kept before the oldest is deleted.
settings.logs.saved-monitoring-failed: The log file settings were saved, the monitoring settings were not:
settings.logs.write.hint: Writes the nginx error, stream and access logs to /data/nginx/logs and rotates them daily. The access log is also written while traffic statistics are on.
settings.monitoring.both-off.confirm: Turn off visitor IPs and unique visitors?
settings.monitoring.retention.hint: {min} to {max} days. Per-minute data is kept for 24 hours, hourly data for this many days.
settings.monitoring.retention.invalid: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}
settings.monitoring.show-ips.confirm.bod: Saving deletes every stored visitor IP address. The counts per host, country and network are kept.
settings.monitoring.show-ips.confirm.ite: Every stored visitor IP address (the counts per host, country and network are kept)
settings.monitoring.show-ips.hint: Stores visitor IP addresses per hour to list the top IPs. Off by default for privacy; turning it off deletes the stored IPs. Countries and networks are counted either way.
settings.monitoring.traffic.confirm.body: No access log is read and nothing new is stored. Statistics of up to the last {days} days are stored; they are kept until they age out.
settings.monitoring.traffic.hint: Writes the nginx access log and counts requests per host, status, country and network for the Monitoring page. Off: no access log is read and nothing new is stored. Stored statistics are kept until they age out, unless you delete them when switching off.
settings.monitoring.unique-visitors.conf: Saving deletes every stored visitor hash. Unique visitor counts are no longer available, the request counts are kept.
Every stored visitor hash (unique visitor counts are no longer available)
settings.monitoring.unique-visitors.hint: Stores a keyed hash of each visitor IP per host and day to count unique visitors. Turning it off deletes them.
settings.monitoring.visitors-cap: Visitor limit per host and day
settings.monitoring.visitors-cap.hint: {min} to {max}. A host that reaches the limit on a day stops counting new visitors for that day and shows the count with a plus sign.
settings.monitoring.visitors-cap.invalid: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}
settings.network.trust-cloudflare.hint: Fetches the Cloudflare IP ranges, refreshes them regularly and trusts them, so nginx sees the real client IPs behind Cloudflare. Read the Cloudflare notes in the README first.
settings.network.trusted-ips.hint: One IPv4/IPv6 address or CIDR range per line. Requests from these addresses may pass the real client IP in X-Forwarded-For, for example from a load balancer or tunnel in front of NPMpro.
settings.network.trusted-ips.invalid: Line {line}: not a valid IPv4/IPv6 address or CIDR range.
settings.runtime.locked.reason.goaccess: GoAccess reads the log files, so {env} keeps them on.
settings.runtime.locked.reason.goaccess-: GoAccess reads the log files, so the GoAccess report keeps them on.
settings.runtime.locked.reason.key-size: The key size in {env} is an ECDSA curve, so the key type stays ECDSA. For RSA, also set ACME_KEY_TYPE=rsa.
settings.runtime.locked.reason.must-stap: Must-Staple certificates need OCSP stapling, so {env} keeps it on.
settings.runtime.locked.reason.ocsp-stap: Must-Staple needs OCSP stapling, which {env} turns off.
settings.runtime.number.invalid: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}
